content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C — Termination for convenience), fallback target.**

What I found across the whole document:

- **§4.1 (p0024)** — one-year term, auto-renewing annually, terminable "by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice." This gives the Company a 90-day convenience/non-renewal right (fallback element 1 met), and HDI's mirror right operates only to defeat renewal at an anniversary, on the full 90 days (fallback elements 3 and 4 met). No walk-away trigger: the term is not multi-year and HDI's notice is not shorter than 90 days.
- **§4.2(a)–(c) (p0026, p0028, p0029)** — the material failure. A **Company-only** Termination Payment equal to half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments, with no reciprocal HDI payment. Against §3.1 fees (30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month), that charge runs multiples of three months' fees, so it breaks the fallback cap.
- **§1.6 (p0011)** — "terminate this Agreement without penalty" is a for-cause remedy for a late launch only; it does not supply a convenience right or cure the fee.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`, minimality clean): a single surgical replacement of the payment formula in §4.2(a) with a three-month fee measure — the notice architecture, which already sits at fallback, is left untouched rather than upgraded to the preferred 30-day/pro-rata-refund wording.
